description.en:
Between 1892 to 1893, Rizal Fr. Pablo Pastells, S.J. had an intellectually vigorous exchange of letters. The latter was determined to make Rizal return to the Catholic faith. Rizal exposed the Church’s abuse of power in his writings and was excommunicated after joining the freemasons. Rizal gave Fr. Pastells a terracotta sculpture of San Pablo el Ermitano or Saint Paul of Thebes who fled from Roman persecution and became the first Christian hermit in Catholic Church history. On February 2, 1893, Fr. Pastells acknowledged the gift and took it as Rizal’s heart had remained Christian, despite his rebellious ideas. Rizal replied that Fr. Pastells should not consider his art work an unconscious confession and that creative expression does not equate to belief. Rather, his sculpture reflects his respect for others’ faith without subscribing to it himself.

In creating this statuette, Rizal used sap from the bakhaw tree as a binder for the palm tree leaves' tunic of St. Paul. The piece is currently exhibited in the Rizal Gallery of the National Museum of Fine Arts.

## References

“Misyon ng mga Hesuwitas sa Pilipinas.”

Letter to Dr. Rizal. 2 February 1893. Typescript, National Historical Commission of the Philippines.

Palma, Celestino. Jose Rizal, Sculptor. Reyes Publishing, 2020.
description.fil:
Sa pagitan ng 1892 at 1893, nagkaroon si Rizal at si Padre Pablo Pastells, S.J. ng masiglang palitan ng liham sa larangan ng isip. Determinado ang huli na pabalikin si Rizal sa pananampalatayang Katoliko. Ibinuyangyang ni Rizal ang pang-aabuso ng Simbahan sa kapangyarihan sa kanyang mga akda at itiniwalag matapos sumapi sa mga mason. Ibinigay ni Rizal kay Padre Pastells ang isang eskulturang terracotta ni San Pablo el Ermitano o San Pablo ng Thebes, na tumakas sa pag-uusig ng mga Romano at naging unang Kristiyanong ermitanyo sa kasaysayan ng Simbahang Katoliko. Noong 2 Pebrero 1893, kinilala ni Padre Pastells ang handog at itinuring itong patunay na nanatiling Kristiyano ang puso ni Rizal, sa kabila ng kanyang mapaghimagsik na kaisipan. Tumugon si Rizal na hindi dapat ituring ni Padre Pastells ang kanyang sining bilang isang di-sinasadyang pagtatapat at na ang malikhaing pagpapahayag ay hindi katumbas ng pananalig. Bagkus, sumasalamin ang kanyang eskultura sa kanyang paggalang sa pananampalataya ng iba nang hindi niya ito sinasapi.

Sa paggawa ng estatwilyang ito, gumamit si Rizal ng dagta mula sa punong bakhaw bilang pampatibay sa tunikang dahon ng palma ni San Pablo. Nakatanghal sa kasalukuyan ang piyesa sa Rizal Gallery ng National Museum of Fine Arts.

## Mga Sanggunian

“Misyon ng mga Hesuwitas sa Pilipinas.”

Letter to Dr. Rizal. 2 February 1893. Typescript, National Historical Commission of the Philippines.

Palma, Celestino. Jose Rizal, Sculptor. Reyes Publishing, 2020.
description.de:
Zwischen 1892 und 1893 führten Rizal und Pater Pablo Pastells, S.J., einen geistig lebhaften Briefwechsel. Pastells war entschlossen, Rizal zum katholischen Glauben zurückzuführen. Rizal legte in seinen Schriften den Machtmissbrauch der Kirche offen und wurde nach seinem Beitritt zu den Freimaurern exkommuniziert. Rizal schenkte Pater Pastells eine Terrakottaskulptur des San Pablo el Ermitano, des heiligen Paulus von Theben, der der römischen Verfolgung entfloh und zum ersten christlichen Eremiten der katholischen Kirchengeschichte wurde. Am 2. Februar 1893 bestätigte Pater Pastells den Empfang des Geschenks und nahm es als Zeichen dafür, dass Rizals Herz trotz seiner aufsässigen Ideen christlich geblieben sei. Rizal erwiderte, Pater Pastells solle sein Kunstwerk nicht für ein unbewusstes Bekenntnis halten; schöpferischer Ausdruck sei nicht dasselbe wie Glaube. Seine Skulptur bezeuge vielmehr seinen Respekt für den Glauben anderer, ohne dass er ihn selbst teile.

Für diese Statuette verwendete Rizal Harz des Bakhaw-Baumes als Bindemittel für die Tunika des heiligen Paulus aus Palmblättern. Das Stück ist derzeit in der Rizal-Galerie des National Museum of Fine Arts ausgestellt.

## Literatur

“Misyon ng mga Hesuwitas sa Pilipinas.”
